Usually the non-dominant hand holds one lightly between thumb and fingertips, palm up, so that the palm becomes the resonating chamber; resting it on the fingernail makes the sound clearer. The dominant hand holds the other with a firmer grip, near its end like a drumstick, and strikes the middle of the resting stick with that end. By tradition the striking stick is called the 'male' and the resting one the 'female', even when the two are identical. A beginner can fix the position of the resting stick first and then practise single strokes; for a roll, hold one between the thumb and the first two fingers and move it back and forth with an alternating pressure, close against the resonating stick.
